summary: A technology strategy carries a [stated FCFA 1,105bn envelope](2025-02-24-new-deal-1105-billion-investment) across twelve programmes to 2034, above a [digital council](2025-10-03-techafricanews-national-digital-council) with no published output and a [steering committee](2026-08-03-senegal-government-enterprise-architecture-dpi-sovereignty) not yet operating.
developments:
The strategy launched in February 2025 with the stated envelope across twelve priority programmes to 2034; the dollar equivalent in circulation rests on an undated conversion and is not a second figure ([envelope](2025-02-24-new-deal-1105-billion-investment), [strategy](2025-02-27 Senegal unveils New Deal Technologique digital transformation strategy)).

A national digital council was inaugurated in October 2025 with twenty members, its mandate covering personal-data protection and cybersecurity advice, and no published output is held ([council](2025-10-03-techafricanews-national-digital-council), [projects](2026-03-24-lesoleil-sonko-projets-structurants)).

A digital governance steering committee was created in March 2026 and was still stated to be operational in the near future five months later ([committee](2026-08-03-senegal-government-enterprise-architecture-dpi-sovereignty)).

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence strategy](2026-07-26-seneweb-ia-afrique-senegal-traine) was adopted in 2023 on six orientations, and a [head-of-state instruction](2026-07-29-senegal-conseil-des-ministres-29-juillet-2026) now calls for a development plan whose relation to it is unestablished.
developments:
The strategy was adopted in 2023 on six orientations. It predates the reporting window so it is not movement, and its first appearance corrected an earlier record that had held there was no published strategy at all ([strategy](2026-07-26-seneweb-ia-afrique-senegal-traine)).

A council of ministers communiqué records a head-of-state instruction for a national development plan, and whether it supersedes, implements or replaces the 2023 strategy is unestablished ([instruction](2026-07-29-senegal-conseil-des-ministres-29-juillet-2026)).

A readiness assessment records an ethics committee as planned; the assessment is dated 2025 with no month and the full report is not held ([committee](2026-07-26-seneweb-ia-afrique-senegal-traine)).

summary: A [national data strategy](2026-07-20-senegal-cdp-saly-atelier-projet-loi-protection-donnees) is cited as adopted and as the frame requiring the data-protection bill to be re-levelled, and a [blueprint for value creation through data](2026-07-06-wearetech-data-ai-governance-blueprint) is at workshop stage.
developments:
The strategy is cited as adopted, with its adoption date unestablished, and it is the frame against which the personal-data bill is being re-levelled. Its first appearance in the base is a coverage gain rather than a policy move ([strategy](2026-07-20-senegal-cdp-saly-atelier-projet-loi-protection-donnees)).

A ministry and partner workshop over two days in July 2026 identified priority sectors for a data and artificial-intelligence governance blueprint, and no published blueprint, date or budget is on file ([blueprint](2026-07-06-wearetech-data-ai-governance-blueprint), [governance](2026-05-26-techafricanews-smart-africa-data-governance)).

progress: Mixed, a revision bill in finalisation while the law in force has stood eighteen years unamended through a breach of the identity directorate
summary: The [personal data law of 2008](2026-07-16 Data Protection Laws of Senegal (reference summary)) has stood eighteen years unamended, and a [revision bill](2026-07-20-senegal-cdp-saly-atelier-projet-loi-protection-donnees) was taken to a two-day workshop to finalise it with its implementing decree.
developments:
The law was promulgated in January 2008 and came into force in 2014, and no amending law is found. It did not move through the February 2026 breach of the national identity directorate ([law](2026-07-16 Data Protection Laws of Senegal (reference summary)), [modernisation](2026-03-27-aps-donnees-personnelles-legislation-moderniser)).

A workshop was convened to finalise the revision bill and its implementing decree; the source is proxy-dated, so the workshop's own date is unknown and must not be rendered as July 2026 ([bill](2026-07-20-senegal-cdp-saly-atelier-projet-loi-protection-donnees)).

The national data strategy is the frame requiring the bill to be re-levelled, so the revision is being written to a strategy rather than to the breach.

summary: A [critical-infrastructure protection law was adopted unanimously](2026-08-20-seneweb-loi-securite-numerique-adoption) on 20 August 2026, and both the [bill text and the inter-commission report](2026-08-20-senegal-rapport-intercommission-projet-loi-25-2026-iic) on it are now held.
developments:
The Assembly adopted the law unanimously ([adoption](2026-08-20-seneweb-loi-securite-numerique-adoption), [detail](2026-08-17-senegal-critical-infrastructure-bill-ministry-details), [safeguard](2026-08-14-senegal-moves-to-safeguard-digital-infrastructure)). Every provision reaching the base through the news accounts is the ministry's own description and the enacted text is not held; the base held nothing on this workstream at the window's start ([cooperation](2026-07-15 Senegal pushes stronger cybersecurity cooperation to protect critical infrastructure), [security](2026-08-14-senegal-critical-infrastructure-cybersecurity-bill), [digital security](2026-08-14-senegal-moves-to-strengthen-critical-infrastructure-and-digital-security)).

The bill's own text and the parliamentary inter-commission report on it are both held, so the base can read the provisions and the committee's reading of them rather than the tabling alone ([bill](2026-08-20-senegal-rapport-intercommission-projet-loi-25-2026-iic), [text](2026-07-02-senegal-projet-loi-25-2026-infrastructures-information-critiques), [hosting](2026-08-20-aps-senegal-hebergement-donnees-personnelles-pleniere), [continuity](2026-08-20-aps-senegal-khady-sarr-cybersecurite-continuite-soins)).

During the debate the Assembly's first vice-president argued cybersecurity must become a standing administrative culture rather than a compliance exercise, calling for mandatory staff training and minimum device-security standards — an account of where the state's own practice stands rather than of what the law requires ([culture](2026-08-20-el-malick-ndiaye-cybersecurite-culture-administrative)).

summary: A [bill on a media and social-network regulator](2025-01-24-draft-law-media-regulator) was presented in January 2025 covering digital platforms and online media, and no source has moved it since.
developments:
The draft was presented with the broadcasting regulator and its scope covers digital platforms, social networks and traditional and online media ([bill](2025-01-24-draft-law-media-regulator)).

Nothing in the base has moved it since January 2025. A ministry legal adviser separately states on the record that the state has worked on social-media regulation since 2024, which is the first dating of the workstream the base holds and does not name the bill ([workstream](2026-07-27-ucak-reseaux-sociaux-intelligence-artificielle-defis)).

summary: A four-country comparative study found [no artificial-intelligence-specific legislation in force or in draft](2026-08-10-grain-west-africa-ai-governance-comparative-study), and the strategy stack and a planned ethics committee carry the field instead.
developments:
The study searched in August 2026 and found no artificial-intelligence-specific instrument on record; it rates a neighbour's strategy the most advanced of the four on inclusion and data governance ([study](2026-08-10-grain-west-africa-ai-governance-comparative-study)).

What the country holds instead is a 2023 strategy, an instruction for a development plan, a planned ethics committee and a non-binding regional guideline set — four policy artefacts and no binding rule.

summary: A [bill on computerising civil-status management](2025-08-01-anec-senegal-digitalisation-etat-civil-aliou-sall) remains listed among outstanding steps, validated but not enacted, and the register-reconstitution decree is likewise unsigned.
developments:
The bill appears among outstanding steps in the agency's own August 2025 presentation and again in the June 2026 programme closing report ([bill](2025-08-01-anec-senegal-digitalisation-etat-civil-aliou-sall), [closure](2026-06-29-aps-nekkal-avancees-modernisation-etat-civil)).

Validated is not enacted. The digitisation programme it would govern has meanwhile closed its external financing, deployed software across most centres and loaded millions of records, so the legal basis trails the system by a wide margin.

summary: The protection authority signed a [cooperation convention with its Benin counterpart](2026-04-17-benin-senegal-apdp-cdp-convention) in April 2026, and no workplan, budget or first joint action has been reported since.
developments:
The convention was signed at the counterpart's headquarters ([convention](2026-04-17-benin-senegal-apdp-cdp-convention)).

No workplan, budget or joint action has followed it. The authority operates under a law that has stood unamended since 2008 and did not move through the identity-directorate breach, so its cross-border cooperation is running ahead of its own domestic instrument.

summary: A [national online child-protection action plan](2026-07-24-lesoleil-plan-national-protection-enfants-en-ligne) was put in place on nine axes, and the plan itself is unpublished.
developments:
The telecommunications ministry put the plan in place on nine axes, the named mechanisms being a focal-point network, a rapid reporting system, digital education in schools and campaigns in national languages ([plan](2026-07-24-lesoleil-plan-national-protection-enfants-en-ligne)).

The plan is unpublished, so the axes are known only through the description of them. It is the only protective instrument in this unit that reached implementation during the window, against a data-protection law still under revision.

summary: Statistical directors-general [approved regional methodological guides](2026-07-31-ecowas-statistical-harmonization) at a Dakar meeting and named national legal instruments as the follow-through owed, and [six states adopted non-binding artificial-intelligence guidelines](2026-07-09-wearetech-six-francophone-ai-governance-framework).
developments:
The guides were approved at the close of the Dakar meeting, and the directors' own recommendation names adoption of national legal instruments as the step the country owes ([guides](2026-07-31-ecowas-statistical-harmonization), [harmonisation](2026-07-28-cote-divoire-ecowas-statistical-harmonisation)).

The artificial-intelligence guidelines were adopted by six francophone West African states on the margins of a global dialogue. They are led by an advocacy organisation rather than a state or bloc secretariat, with no compliance mechanism, budget or review cycle named ([guidelines](2026-07-09-wearetech-six-francophone-ai-governance-framework)).

Both instruments are agreed at regional level and both leave the binding step to national law that has not been taken.

summary: The digital minister signed the [founding agreement of a global artificial-intelligence cooperation body](2026-07-19-senegal-waico-founding) in Shanghai, and no obligation, contribution or ratification step is reported.
developments:
The founding agreement was signed in July 2026 ([membership](2026-07-19-senegal-waico-founding)).

Nothing states what membership requires of the country. It sits alongside a presentation of a national artificial-intelligence programme in Tokyo and exploratory talks in Washington and Beijing: the diplomacy is broad and none of it has yet produced an instrument the base can read.

The bilateral digital-cooperation memorandum signed at Dakar on 12 June 2026 held its first steering-committee session at Banjul on 29 August 2026, settling four priorities — infrastructure and interoperability, cyber resilience, capacity building and regulatory harmonisation — with rural electronic-government access named among the work ([steering committee](2026-08-29-senegal-gambie-feuille-route-numerique-commune)).

No timetable, budget or named deliverable is attached to any of the four priorities, so what the committee has agreed is a list of headings.

summary: [Free roaming with Togo and Benin took effect](2026-04-27-techreviewafrica-senegal-togo-benin-free-roaming) in April 2026, implementing a regional regulation adopted in December 2017.
developments:
It took effect at Lomé on 24 April 2026 ([roaming](2026-04-27-techreviewafrica-senegal-togo-benin-free-roaming)).

The regulation behind it was adopted in December 2017 and applied only now, which is the finding: the instrument was not the constraint, and nothing on file says what was.

summary: A second monitoring committee set a [three-month roadmap for customs data exchange with Gambia](2026-07-20-thepoint-gra-senegal-customs-ict-transit) on 17 July 2026, agreed at operational level rather than by treaty.
developments:
The roadmap clock started on 17 July 2026 ([roadmap](2026-07-20-thepoint-gra-senegal-customs-ict-transit)).

It was agreed between customs administrations at operational level rather than by treaty, so there is no ratified basis for the transfer of the data it would move, and the protection authority is not named in it.

summary: An [inventory of state information systems was launched](2026-08-03-senegal-government-enterprise-architecture-dpi-sovereignty) at a July 2026 workshop alongside interim diagnostic results, and the inventory carries no scope, deadline or publication commitment.
developments:
Interim diagnostic results were presented and the inventory launched at a workshop on 29 July 2026, implemented by the state digital agency with donor programme funding ([architecture](2026-08-03-senegal-government-enterprise-architecture-dpi-sovereignty), [projects](2026-03-24-lesoleil-sonko-projets-structurants), [agenda](2026-07-31-senegal-advances-digital-transformation-agenda-with-government-enterprise-architecture-project)).

The inventory is the load-bearing commitment: without it there is no list of the systems any interoperability platform would have to reach. It is now under way and carries no scope, deadline or publication commitment.

summary: A [decree on classified defence procurement](2026-04-22-senegal-decret-2026-807-marches-secret-defense) was signed in April 2026, its stated direction control rather than expansion because administrations were invoking the classification improperly.
developments:
The decree was signed on 22 April 2026 and published in the official journal a week later ([decree](2026-04-22-senegal-decret-2026-807-marches-secret-defense)).

The accompanying report says administrations were invoking the classification improperly, so the instrument narrows a route that had been used to avoid open procurement. It is relevant here because the state's own diagnosis locates the blockage on critical-infrastructure cybersecurity in procurement rather than in budget or capability.

progress: Mixed, a ministry vote of FCFA 81.06bn announced for 2026 while the civil-status agency's own budget had still not been notified in August
summary: The [2026 ministry budget was set at FCFA 81.06bn](2026-01-01-sen-2026-digital-ministry-investment) with about 60 per cent to investment, while the [the civil-status agency 2026 appropriation had not been notified](2026-08-17-senegal-anec-kaolack-civil-registry-budget-gap) by August.
developments:
The 2026 ministry figure is an announcement rather than an appropriation: the record's own flags read unclear on stage and partial on scope, and the source says the budget was set without stating tabled or enacted ([vote](2026-01-01-sen-2026-digital-ministry-investment)).

At sector level only the 2024 machine budget record exists; the 2025 figure of FCFA 31.1bn is source-stated in committee reporting and is not held as a budget record, and nothing at sector level exists for 2026 ([sector](2024-12-20-digitalbusinessafrica-mctn-budget-2025-vs-2024), [baseline](2024-01-01-sen-2024-mctn-economie-numerique)).

The civil-status agency's director-general said on 17 August 2026 that its 2026 budget had still not been notified, and named that as the constraint on the pace of the regional phase of civil-registry digitisation ([agency](2026-08-17-senegal-anec-kaolack-civil-registry-budget-gap)).

summary: A [memorandum with a United Nations development programme](2026-04-16-techafricanews-undp-senegal-mou) was signed with the digital ministry, with no value, duration, workplan or deliverables and the text not held.
developments:
The memorandum was signed in April 2026 ([memorandum](2026-04-16-techafricanews-undp-senegal-mou)).

Nothing about it is published beyond the signature. The same programme separately funds an equipment tender for a parliamentary system, which is the only concrete activity the base can attach to the relationship.

summary: A [regional bank loan for digital transformation of public services](2026-03-26-iati-xm-dac-46021-2026028-senegal-digital-transformation-public-services) was committed in March 2026, a [digital economy acceleration project](2026-02-17-wearetech-world-bank-paens) was realigned to the technology strategy, and a [US$10m foundation grant](2025-09-29 Gates Foundation fuels Senegal's digital transformation with $10M) is approved and undisbursed.
developments:
The regional bank loan was committed on 26 March 2026 ([loan](2026-03-26-iati-xm-dac-46021-2026028-senegal-digital-transformation-public-services)).

A portfolio review realigned the acceleration project to the technology strategy and validated first-half 2026 milestones; the two amounts on record for the project are not reconciled in the base ([review](2026-02-17-wearetech-world-bank-paens), [project](2023-02-09-wb-sen-001-senegal-digital-economy-acceleration-project)).

The foundation grant of US$10m was committed on the margins of a United Nations session and is approved and not disbursed in the deal record ([grant](2025-09-29 Gates Foundation fuels Senegal's digital transformation with $10M)); the same item carries a 2025 to 2034 requirement figure that is a need rather than a commitment ([grant](2025-09-29 Gates Foundation fuels Senegal's digital transformation with $10M), [deal](2025-01-01-gates-foundation-sen-2025-new-deal-technologique-bw05)).

summary: A [US$137m mobile-money debt raise](2025-06-30-techcabal-wave-137m-debt) closed in June 2025, a [tower operator committed US$150m](2026-07-20-helios-towers-150-million-senegal-digital-infrastructure) on a presidential account, and a [EUR 270m network facility](2026-07-13 EBRD Extends €270m Financing to Yas for Kenya, Senegal Network Expansion) was extended.
developments:
The debt raise is the largest private-sector financing in the base after the Chinese credit lines, closed one month before the window opened and unmoved since ([debt](2025-06-30-techcabal-wave-137m-debt), [investment](2025-01-01-bii-sen-001-wave-mobile-money-debt-investment-mobile)).

The tower commitment traces solely to the Presidency; trade press moved from plans to commitment in a day with no new evidence, and the operator already ran 1,479 sites in the country in the first quarter of 2026 ([towers](2026-07-20-helios-towers-150-million-senegal-digital-infrastructure), [commitment](2026-07-21-helios-towers-commits-150m-to-senegal-expansion)).

The network facility is a bank's first project in the country and its first sub-Saharan local-currency structure, and the country's share is not disaggregated ([facility](2026-07-13 EBRD Extends €270m Financing to Yas for Kenya, Senegal Network Expansion)). A pre-seed and seed fund was announced on a conference stage with no first close, limited partners, fund manager or deployment held ([fund](2026-07-07-techcabal-catalyst-derfj-50m-fund)).

summary: A [subsea cable landing station was commissioned](2026-02-23-techafricanews-sonatel-2africa-cable) in December 2025, and a [second cable landing](2026-05-23 Orange-backed subsea cable to connect Nigeria, 19 other countries) was announced in May 2026 with no landing-site, financing or contract detail.
developments:
The landing station was commissioned in December 2025; the base holds a month-precision event date and no day ([station](2026-02-23-techafricanews-sonatel-2africa-cable)).

The second cable was announced at a continental summit in May 2026 and no landing-site, financing or contract detail is held for the country's leg ([cable](2026-05-23 Orange-backed subsea cable to connect Nigeria, 19 other countries)).

An internet exchange point reactivation was announced in a state and operator partnership in March 2025 and is the only source in the base naming the exchange ([exchange](2025-03-26-senum-sonatel-partnership)).

summary: The incumbent operator [committed to one million new fibre sockets](2026-04-22-techafricanews-sonatel-ftth-annual-report) between 2026 and 2028, and a [mobile latency measurement](2026-07-21-seneweb-latence-mobile-connectivite) covering January to July 2026 is the first the base holds.
developments:
The fibre commitment was set out with full-year 2025 results in April 2026 ([results](2026-04-22-techafricanews-sonatel-ftth-annual-report)).

The latency measurement covers January to July 2026 and no prior figure for the country is held, so it establishes a baseline rather than a direction ([latency](2026-07-21-seneweb-latence-mobile-connectivite)).

Both figures are the operator's and a measurement firm's; no regulator series on quality of service is held for this unit.

summary: [Rural household internet access](2026-03-09-connectingafrica-free-internet-cyber-risks) was stated at end-2025 against fourth-generation coverage reaching 97 per cent of the population, so the shortfall is usage rather than coverage.
developments:
The rural figure sits against fourth-generation coverage reaching 97 per cent of the population in 2025, which makes it a usage gap rather than a coverage gap ([access](2026-03-09-connectingafrica-free-internet-cyber-risks)).

That distinction decides what would close it. Coverage obligations and tower financing do not reach a household that is covered and not connected, and the instruments recorded elsewhere in this report — the connectivity project, the device programme, the affordability measures — are the ones that would.

summary: A [five-year satellite operating authorisation](2026-02-24-sen-aps-starlink-autorisation-cinq-ans) was granted in February 2026, a [teleport gateway](2026-07-10-techafricanews-sonatel-gandoul-oneweb) is in service, and the [universal connectivity project](2026-04-09-lesoleil-connectivite-universelle-tournee) slipped through the first half.
developments:
The authorisation runs five years, with commercial launch about 4 February 2026 and the country the operator's twenty-sixth African market; the regulator separately warned against illegal wireless resale ([authorisation](2026-02-24-sen-aps-starlink-autorisation-cinq-ans), [framework](2026-02-05-sen-artp-starlink-cadre-autorisation), [warning](2026-04-02-senegal-artp-illegal-wifi-warning)).

A teleport satellite gateway is in service; the source states no commissioning date so the publication date is used ([gateway](2026-07-10-techafricanews-sonatel-gandoul-oneweb)).

The universal connectivity project opened a deployment tour in April 2026; the target was restated between February and April and the first half closed with nothing published ([tour](2026-04-09-lesoleil-connectivite-universelle-tournee), [deployment](2026-04-11-lesoleil-alioune-sall-kolda-starlink), [kits](2026-02-04-lesoleil-starlink-5000-kits)).

summary: The [national data centre](2025-09-18-bagwandeen-huawei-african-data-sovereignty-georgetown) was commissioned in June 2021 at US$18.2m, externally financed and built, and a [second commercial facility](2025-01-23 PAIX Data Centres breaks ground on Dakar data center) broke ground in January 2025.
developments:
The national facility's figures come from an academic analysis citing secondary sources, with no domestic primary held ([centre](2025-09-18-bagwandeen-huawei-african-data-sovereignty-georgetown), [financing](2021-01-01-eximbank-cn-sen-003-diamniadio-data-centre-restructuring-and-smart)).

A commercial facility broke ground in January 2025; its target year has not expired, so it is not recorded as stalled ([groundbreaking](2025-01-23 PAIX Data Centres breaks ground on Dakar data center), [build](2025-01-27-paix-dakar-data-center-connectingafrica)).

The count of data centres operating in the country reaches the base only as a continental reference-study figure at mid-2025, cited and not absorbed; no domestic primary count and no capacity figure is held ([count](2026-08-03-afrique-data-centers-souverainete-donnees)).

progress: Mixed, one sovereign-cloud partner reported as deployed and tested while another signed two years earlier has produced no build
summary: A [sovereign cloud built with a Chinese vendor](2026-04-29-africabusinessinsight-senegal-alibaba-sovereign-cloud) is in testing with equipment installed and verified, while a [memorandum with a hyperscaler](2024-10-04 Senegal launches sovereign cloud initiative with Google) signed in October 2024 has produced no build.
developments:
The minister states the Chinese-partner infrastructure is deployed and tested, equipment installed and verified. No contract, value, hosting-term, exit or data-access terms are reported ([cloud](2026-04-29-africabusinessinsight-senegal-alibaba-sovereign-cloud), [sovereignty](2026-08-03-afrique-data-centers-souverainete-donnees)).

The hyperscaler memorandum was signed in October 2024 and no build, siting, capacity or spend was reported in the twelve months to August 2026. The base does not establish how the two arrangements relate ([memorandum](2024-10-04 Senegal launches sovereign cloud initiative with Google)).

Cloud residency zones in operator data centres have been in service since May 2024 and are the residency substitute for a country with no full cloud region ([residency](2024-05-30 Orange and AWS partner to deliver cloud services in Morocco and Senegal)).

progress: Mixed, a critical-infrastructure law adopted while the country still has neither a national cybersecurity agency nor a national response team
summary: A [national computer emergency response team](2026-08-14-senegal-moves-to-safeguard-digital-infrastructure) is provided for in a bill and does not yet exist, and the [procurement route](2026-08-18-digitalbusiness-senegal-cybastion-mou-cybersecurite) is where the state's own diagnosis locates the blockage.
developments:
A named expert stated in February 2026 that the country has neither a national cybersecurity agency nor a national response team, and no evidence was found that either has since been established; the team is provided for in a bill before the Assembly ([team](2026-08-14-senegal-moves-to-safeguard-digital-infrastructure)).

The state's own diagnosis locates the blockage in procurement rather than in budget or capability, and a memorandum with a foreign cybersecurity supplier was reported in August 2026 whose text, scope and value are not published ([memorandum](2026-08-18-digitalbusiness-senegal-cybastion-mou-cybersecurite), [procurement](2026-07-30-arcop-cybersecurite-marches-infrastructures-critiques)).

The international cybersecurity index score held is the 2024 edition, a reference figure cited and not absorbed, and it predates the entire breach run ([index](2026-07-15 Senegal pushes stronger cybersecurity cooperation to protect critical infrastructure)). Police cybercrime figures are reported alongside an international estimate of Africa-wide losses, with neither the recording basis nor a clear-up rate stated ([offences](2026-08-17-senegal-autorite-nationale-cybersecurite)).

summary: [Three state systems were breached](2026-08-20-seneweb-sonko-cyberattack-auditions) and the Assembly announced hearings of the technical services and the agencies hit, a day after the critical-infrastructure law's adoption.
developments:
The treasury breach carries month precision only, and no technical accounting has been published for any of the three ([breaches](2026-03-09-connectingafrica-free-internet-cyber-risks), [identity file](2026-02-11-zataz-senegal-frappe-fichier-identite), [maturity](2026-02-12-darkreading-senegal-breach-security-maturity)).

On 20 August 2026, a day after the law's adoption, the Assembly's president announced hearings of the state technical services and of the agencies hit, naming the file-automation directorate and the tax and domains directorate. Neither the number of further incidents nor their dates is stated, so three is the count the base can still support ([hearings](2026-08-20-seneweb-sonko-cyberattack-auditions)).

That the legislature moved to hearings only after the law passed is the sequence the record shows.

summary: An [enterprise-architecture account names interoperability as a standing challenge](2026-08-03-senegal-government-enterprise-architecture-dpi-sovereignty) with platforms still siloed sixteen months after launch, and no source records the first phase completing on its end-2025 target.
developments:
The platform launched in April 2025 with a first phase targeted at end-2025, and no held source records that phase completing ([platform](2025-04-22-lesoleil-interoperability-platform), [update](2025-09-19-techafricanews-interoperability-update)).

Sixteen months on, the government's own enterprise-architecture account names interoperability as a standing challenge and describes platforms as still siloed ([architecture](2026-08-03-senegal-government-enterprise-architecture-dpi-sovereignty)).

A separate climate-transparency data platform launched in July 2026 on 42 months of external funding, and the ministry names the defect directly: gaps in availability, quality, harmonisation and inter-sectoral sharing ([climate](2026-07-22-seneweb-cbit-donnees-climatiques), [project](2025-08-11-gef-senegal-cbit-etf-project-document)).

summary: A convention commits the [state digital agency and the health-cover platform to interconnect](2026-07-24-senum-sa-sen-csu-partenariat-couverture-maladie), with no enrolment target, go-live date or named data-sharing instrument.
developments:
The convention was announced in July 2026 committing the two bodies to interconnect their platforms ([convention](2026-07-24-senum-sa-sen-csu-partenariat-couverture-maladie), [partnership](2026-07-22-senum-sen-csu-convention)).

No enrolment target, go-live date or named data-sharing instrument accompanies it, and the personal-data commitment is an intention rather than something referred to the regulator.

The ministry has meanwhile begun building a single patient record ahead of the law meant to govern its confidentiality and transfer, so health data is being joined up in two places at once with no instrument governing either.

summary: A [two-day workshop opened in July 2026](2026-07-23-guichet-unique-acces-services-sociaux-senegal) to diagnose existing systems and settle interoperability and data governance for a unified social-protection information system.
developments:
It covers five named social programmes, and no budget, timeline or lead technical agency is reported ([workshop](2026-07-23-guichet-unique-acces-services-sociaux-senegal), [system](2026-07-23-lesoleil-systeme-information-interoperable)).

Data governance is an output of the workshop rather than an input to it, which is the same ordering the health interconnection and the digital addressing relaunch show: the systems are being designed and the rules that would govern them are being written afterwards.

summary: [Identity card production resumed](2026-04-07-aps-daf-reprise-production-cni) on 1 April 2026 after a ransomware breach forced a two-month suspension, and exfiltration is unrebutted.
developments:
Production was suspended on 5 February 2026 and resumed on 1 April ([suspension](2026-02-05-aps-daf-suspension-cni-communique), [resumption](2026-04-07-aps-daf-reprise-production-cni)).

Exfiltration is unrebutted: the directorate's communiqués assert integrity only, never confidentiality. The volume claim appears as both 139 GB and 139 TB across one actor's two artefacts, so even the size of the loss is unestablished ([breach](2026-02-12-darkreading-senegal-breach-security-maturity)).

The data-protection law did not move through the breach, and no technical accounting has been published.

summary: The [externally funded civil-registration modernisation programme closed](2026-06-29-aps-nekkal-avancees-modernisation-etat-civil) at a final steering committee in June 2026 — a programme closure rather than a capability closure.
developments:
The final steering committee was held on 29 June 2026, closing the programme ([closure](2026-06-29-aps-nekkal-avancees-modernisation-etat-civil), [programme](2020-05-07-european-union-sen-2020-nekkal-civil-registration-bw01)).

It is the only European governance instrument on file for the country. The capability it built continues — software is deployed across most centres and millions of records are loaded — but the financing that built it has ended, and the agency running it says its own 2026 budget has not been notified.

progress: Mixed, birth registration coverage advancing while an audit tests the reliability of the paper base the digital register is built on
summary: [Birth registration coverage](2026-08-05-senegal-civil-registration-digitalization-anec) rests on two instruments on different bases, and an [audit of civil registration in 74 communes](2026-07-29-seneweb-etat-civil-74-communes-cour-des-comptes) covering 2018 to 2025 was launched in July 2026.
developments:
The coverage figures come from two instruments on different bases — a census stock figure and a survey coverage rate — which is why they cannot be read as one series ([coverage](2026-08-05-senegal-civil-registration-digitalization-anec)).

The audit mission was launched at Rufisque on 28 July 2026 covering 2018 to 2025. It tests the reliability of the paper base the digital register is built on, and no findings or reporting date are stated ([audit](2026-07-29-seneweb-etat-civil-74-communes-cour-des-comptes)).

An audit of that scope, opened while the register is being loaded, is the right sequence and the one the record most often shows reversed elsewhere in this unit.

summary: [Civil-status software reached 437 of 629 centres](2026-07-21-anec-senegal-etat-davancement-lgec-437-sur-629), [15.3m records are loaded live](2026-07-15 Senegal digitizes more than 15 million birth records in civil registration overhaul), and the [archive totals](2026-06-29-aps-nekkal-avancees-modernisation-etat-civil) are given as two unreconciled figures.
developments:
The deployment figure was given at African Civil Registration Day in August 2026 against a denominator of 629 centres; the agency's director-general frames civil registration as an instrument of sovereignty, and the same agency says its 2026 budget has not been notified ([deployment](2026-08-10-senegal-anec-civil-registry-sovereignty-modernisation), [progress](2026-07-21-anec-senegal-etat-davancement-lgec-437-sur-629), [presentation](2025-08-01-anec-senegal-digitalisation-etat-civil-aliou-sall)).

The live database holds 15.3m records loaded, a subset of archive stock rather than a replacement figure; English coverage calls them birth records where the agency's own term covers all events ([database](2026-07-15 Senegal digitizes more than 15 million birth records in civil registration overhaul)).

The June 2026 closing report gives 10m digitised and 20m indexed as two separate totals, unreconciled with the August 2025 reading ([archive](2026-06-29-aps-nekkal-avancees-modernisation-etat-civil), [agency](2025-08-01-anec-senegal-digitalisation-etat-civil-aliou-sall)). Remediation ran at one region in August 2026 on the agency's own pilot data, with no national completion date stated ([remediation](2026-08-16-senegal-anec-civil-registry-digitisation-remediation-progress)).

summary: A [national digital addressing project was relaunched](2026-08-07-senegal-relaunches-national-digital-addressing-project) at a workshop in August 2026, with no budget, lead implementing agency or pilot geography stated.
developments:
The relaunch workshop opened on 5 August 2026 ([relaunch](2026-08-07-senegal-relaunches-national-digital-addressing-project)).

The government states the project made conceptual and technical progress in earlier years, and the base holds no position for it before the relaunch — so what is being relaunched cannot be measured against what existed.

summary: A [business registration platform](2025-02-04-ninea-business-registration-platform) launched in February 2025 for the enterprise and association identification number, and eighteen months have passed with no update.
developments:
The platform launched in February 2025 ([platform](2025-02-04-ninea-business-registration-platform)).

Eighteen months with no update in the base means the object may have moved without the base holding it, which is a limit on this reading rather than a finding about the platform.

summary: The [single national social register rose from 542,000 to one million households](2025-12-09 Senegal's RNU social registry rises from 542,000 to one million households) over 2024, and no later figure is held.
developments:
The growth was reported in December 2025 and ingested in July 2026, so it is a 2024 event rather than movement in the window ([register](2025-12-09 Senegal's RNU social registry rises from 542,000 to one million households), [brief](2019-05-01 Senegal National Single Registry RNU (IPC-IG research brief 63))).

The unified social-protection information system now being designed would sit above it, and the workshop that opened that design names data governance as an output rather than an input.

summary: A [biometric audit of the public-service headcount](2026-07-20-lesoleil-audit-fonction-publique-enrolement) began enrolment in June 2026 and a [biometric register of artisanal gold miners](2026-08-04-senegal-orpaillage-identification-biometrique) was agreed by convention, neither stating a data-protection provision.
developments:
The headcount audit runs physical and biometric enrolment from 23 June 2026. It is identity infrastructure whose beneficiary is the treasury, and no correction or grievance route is stated for an agent the audit fails to find ([audit](2026-07-20-lesoleil-audit-fonction-publique-enrolement)).

The miners' register was agreed by a convention signed on 30 July 2026 between the mines ministry and the deposits fund; no enrolment target, timetable, cost, host, retention period or regulator role is stated, and the reported design carries no data-protection provision ([register](2026-08-04-senegal-orpaillage-identification-biometrique)).

Two new biometric collections in two months, in a country whose identity directorate was breached in February and whose data-protection law is still under revision.

summary: The country's [share of regional mobile-money transaction volume](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024) rose on the central bank's own 2024 series, and a [super-app was integrated into the rapid-transit network](2026-07-15-wearetech-sonatel-maxit-brt) for ticketing.
developments:
Both ends of the regional share come from the same source's own series rather than from movement in the base, and eleven electronic-money issuers operate in the country ([share](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024)).

A super-app was integrated into the rapid-transit network for ticketing and top-ups; the prior digital-payment figure carries no date, and the network runs up to 300,000 passengers a day ([transit](2026-07-15-wearetech-sonatel-maxit-brt)).

progress: Mixed, the paper fiscal stamp withdrawn in favour of a digital channel while the free tier of that channel was suspended eight days later
summary: The tax authority [withdrew the paper fiscal stamp](2026-07-20-senegal-timbre-fiscal-numerique-sentimbre) on 20 July 2026, and a [provider suspended its free electronic stamp service](2026-07-29-lesoleil-diotali-timbre-fiscal-electronique) on 28 July citing an administrative decision outside its control.
developments:
The withdrawal made the digital service the sole recognised channel. It is removal of the analogue route rather than addition of a digital one: unused paper stamps were exchangeable until 15 August 2026, and no offline or assisted route is stated ([stamp](2026-07-20-senegal-timbre-fiscal-numerique-sentimbre), [channel](2026-07-29-lesoleil-diotali-timbre-fiscal-electronique)).

Eight days later a provider suspended its free tier, citing an administrative decision outside its control. It is the first consumer-cost consequence of state-platform exclusivity the base holds, and it is not stated whether the decision was addressed to that provider or to the distribution channel generally ([suspension](2026-07-29-lesoleil-diotali-timbre-fiscal-electronique)).

A levy on mobile-money transfers was proposed under a recovery plan to raise about FCFA 220bn over three years; both sources post-date the window's start, so the proposal's earlier position cannot be stated ([levy](2025-12-08 GSMA maps the reforms required for Senegal's digital takeoff)).

summary: The ministry [has begun building a single patient record](2026-07-24-coeur-rose-diourbel-loi-sante-digitale) ahead of the law meant to govern confidentiality and transfer, and a [mortality and cause-of-death tool](2026-07-24-lesoleil-anacod3-donnees-mortalite) is in pilot.
developments:
A civil-society call for adoption of a digital-health bill was made at a restitution day in July 2026, and the record notes the ministry has begun building a single patient record accessible to certified structures ahead of that law ([bill](2026-07-24-coeur-rose-diourbel-loi-sante-digitale)).

The mortality and cause-of-death analysis tool was trained on over two days in July 2026. Cause-of-death quality is being worked on inside the health information system rather than through the civil register, which is where the audit and the digitisation programme sit ([tool](2026-07-24-lesoleil-anacod3-donnees-mortalite)).

summary: A [citizen single window](2026-03-27-biometricupdate-e-senegal-portal) was launched and declared operational in March 2026, and a [public procurement platform](2026-07-30-appel-une-plateforme-strategique-a-proteger) carries state acquisition procedures with no onboarding or volume figure published.
developments:
The portal was launched by the prime minister on 24 March 2026 and declared operational, presented alongside a sovereignty cloud, a unified government payment system and a consular platform ([portal](2026-03-27-biometricupdate-e-senegal-portal), [year on](2026-03-19-lesoleil-new-deal-un-an-apres)).

The procurement platform launched in October 2025 to carry state acquisition procedures, and no count of administrations onboarded, procurement volume, availability record or security accreditation is stated ([procurement](2026-07-30-appel-une-plateforme-strategique-a-proteger)).

The telecommunications regulator has deployed eight platforms of its own, sovereignty-framed and with no usage or publication figures held ([regulator](2026-01-28-techafricanews-artp-digital-tools)), and an equipment tender for a parliamentary system opened in August 2026 with no function, scope or go-live on record ([parliament](2026-08-05-senegal-undp-sipop-national-assembly-it-equipment)).

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence factory](2026-08-03-new-deal-technologique-le-senegal-devoile-la-senegal-ai-factory-a-tokyo) was presented in Tokyo, and a [Wolof and French tutor delivered by phone call](2026-07-30-allo-goor-gi-ia-contenus-pedagogiques-certifies) was presented at a national prize ceremony.
developments:
The programme was presented to an international artificial-intelligence process meeting; the topics the delegation discussed — trustworthy-artificial-intelligence governance, compute infrastructure, innovation financing and partnerships — are the things the programme is not yet reported to have ([factory](2026-08-03-new-deal-technologique-le-senegal-devoile-la-senegal-ai-factory-a-tokyo)).

The tutor works over a phone call in Wolof and French, so it reaches users without smartphones or data. No user, pricing, call-cost, contract or evaluation figures are given, and the education ministry's role is asserted by the vendor rather than confirmed by it ([tutor](2026-07-30-allo-goor-gi-ia-contenus-pedagogiques-certifies)).

summary: The [Startup Act labelling process](2026-03-19-lesoleil-new-deal-un-an-apres) launched in the strategy's first year against a 2034 target of more than 500 labelled firms, and no count of labelled startups is held.
developments:
The implementing decree was adopted in January 2025 and the labelling process launched in the strategy's first year; the published target for 2034 is more than 500 and no count is held at any date ([labelling](2026-03-19-lesoleil-new-deal-un-an-apres), [implementation](2025-01-30-startup-law-implementation-phase)).

A corporate mobility platform launched in July 2026, its claimed cost reduction the company's own ([mobility](2026-07-17-senegal-yango-expands-into-corporate-mobility)).

A transit operator and the telecommunications operator signed a super-app partnership in July 2026, described as progressive and eventual throughout with no go-live date or phasing published ([super-app](2026-07-15-wearetech-sonatel-maxit-brt)).

summary: A [digital financial-education project closed](2026-07-24-finance-4-all-senegal-education-financiere-numerique) in July 2026, and the base held nothing on it before the closing item, so its whole life-cycle arrives at once.
developments:
The project closed on 15 July 2026 with a closing workshop the following week ([closure](2026-07-24-finance-4-all-senegal-education-financiere-numerique)).

The base held nothing on it before 24 July 2026, so there is no record of what it did, reached or cost — only that it ended. That is a coverage limit rather than a finding, and it is worth stating because it is the second literacy instrument in this unit whose record is a single item.

summary: A [Digital Schools memorandum](2025-03-12-digital-schools-sonatel-mou) to equip 120 primary schools and train 500 women at seven digital houses stands unchanged across the window.
developments:
The memorandum was signed in March 2025 and the position is identical at both ends of the window ([memorandum](2025-03-12-digital-schools-sonatel-mou)).

It is the only school-level digital-literacy instrument the base holds for this country. Against a national technology strategy running to 2034 and a student-computer programme now under parliamentary inquiry, one unmoved memorandum is the whole of the school record.

summary: The Assembly [voted 129-0 to open a commission of inquiry](2026-08-20-seneweb-etudiant-ordinateur-enquete) into a student-computer programme, over roughly 48 billion FCFA committed since 2017 and 800 defective computers stored unused at a university.
developments:
The inquiry covers alleged breaches of the public procurement code, a guarantee fund of about 2 billion FCFA with a commercial bank, and the defective machines held at the country's main university ([inquiry](2026-08-20-seneweb-etudiant-ordinateur-enquete)).

No device-delivery total, cost per unit or student-reach figure is published for the programme, so the inquiry's envelope is the only quantity the base holds about it — nine years of a flagship access programme whose only measurable number is what it may have cost.

progress: Mixed, a statistics school graduating a large cohort while the national agency presses ministries to absorb them and cloud-engineer training has not started
summary: The [the statistics school 2026 cohort](2026-08-20-lesoleil-ansd-ensae-recrutement) drew students from ten African countries and the national agency used the graduation to press ministries to recruit them, and [sovereign-cloud engineer training has not started](2026-04-29-africabusinessinsight-senegal-alibaba-sovereign-cloud).
developments:
The agency's intervention states an absorption problem without measuring it: no figure is published for how many of the 900 graduates are employed in domestic public statistics ([cohort](2026-08-20-lesoleil-ansd-ensae-recrutement)).

The digital minister states the sovereign-cloud infrastructure is deployed and tested and that training has not started; no contract, value or schedule is held ([training](2026-04-29-africabusinessinsight-senegal-alibaba-sovereign-cloud)).

A US$200m five-year skills commitment announced in September 2019 is the largest single skills commitment in the base, and seven years on the base holds no evidence of delivery ([commitment](2019-01-01-mcf-sen-youngafricaworks-2019-young-africa-works-in-senegal)).

summary: [Two artificial-intelligence research laboratories](2025-01-31-alive-dicentre4ai-ai-labs) launched in January 2025 with three ministers present, and eighteen months have produced no follow-up item.
developments:
They are the only standing artificial-intelligence research infrastructure the base holds for the country, and no follow-up item has entered it in eighteen months ([laboratories](2025-01-31-alive-dicentre4ai-ai-labs)).

A council of ministers communiqué proposes a national research and innovation fund alongside applied research laboratories, and none of the proposals is an adopted instrument ([fund](2026-07-29-senegal-conseil-des-ministres-29-juillet-2026)).

summary: An [advanced-level digital course for blind and partially sighted people](2026-07-06-seneweb-programme-employabilite-non-voyants) launched in July 2026, with no start date for the programme and no funding figure or state role reported.
developments:
The advanced course launched on 6 July 2026 ([course](2026-07-06-seneweb-programme-employabilite-non-voyants)).

The programme's start date is not stated, so the cumulative figure it reports has no start point, and no funding figure or state role is reported. It is the only disability-specific digital instrument in this ledger.

summary: The telecommunications minister put [40 per cent of the population without connectivity](2026-08-20-seneweb-fracture-numerique-40pc) during the critical-infrastructure debate, on a 2024 diagnosis that is not held.
developments:
The figure was stated during the bill's debate and attributed to a 2024 sector diagnosis of coverage gaps and unmet operator obligations. The diagnosis itself is not held, no definition of access is given, and the figure is two years old at the point of its citation ([gap](2026-08-20-seneweb-fracture-numerique-40pc)).

It sits against fourth-generation coverage reaching 97 per cent of the population in 2025 ([coverage](2026-03-09-connectingafrica-free-internet-cyber-risks)), so the two figures are measuring different things and no source reconciles them.

summary: The national statistics agency hosted the [first second-phase peer exchange of an inclusive-data initiative](2026-07-01-gpsdd-midn-dakar-peer-exchange) in Dakar.
developments:
The exchange was hosted in July 2026; the base holds a month-precision date and the exact dates are not published ([exchange](2026-07-01-gpsdd-midn-dakar-peer-exchange)).

The same agency used a graduation ceremony the following month to press ministries to recruit statisticians into sectoral services, so it is convening internationally on inclusive data while stating a staffing problem at home.

summary: The digital minister [pitched the technology strategy in Washington](2026-07-24-new-deal-technologique-senegal-partenariats-washington) with the State Department and the development finance corporation, and an [exploratory meeting with an embassy delegation](2026-08-17-senegal-us-cybersecurity-ai-cooperation) followed in August 2026.
developments:
The Washington working sessions are reported with no date beyond the publication date, and nothing beyond talks is on record ([talks](2026-07-24-new-deal-technologique-senegal-partenariats-washington)).

The August meeting on cybersecurity and artificial-intelligence cooperation is a meeting rather than an instrument: no memorandum, workstream, funding or timetable is reported ([meeting](2026-08-17-senegal-us-cybersecurity-ai-cooperation)).

Against a sovereign-cloud memorandum with an American hyperscaler that has produced no build in nearly two years, the American relationship in this unit is entirely at the discussion stage.

summary: A [strategic partnership with a Chinese vendor](2026-08-19-seneweb-cooperation-sino-senegalaise-ia-huawei) took artificial-intelligence-in-education governance to Beijing in August 2026, and thirteen months on the base holds no evidence the assembly plant exists.
developments:
The partnership was signed a month before the window opened, so it is the baseline rather than news, and thirteen months on nothing establishes that the assembly plant it named exists ([partnership](2026-08-19-seneweb-cooperation-sino-senegalaise-ia-huawei), [accord](2025-06-27-lesoleil-senegal-huawei-accord), [sovereignty](2025-03-27-huawei-partnership-digital-sovereignty)).

A position on media technology cooperation was put at a Sino-African media forum in August 2026, with no instrument, funding or work programme named ([media](2026-08-21-lesoleil-senegal-hubs-africains-ia)).

The sovereign cloud recorded elsewhere in this report is the one Chinese arrangement that has produced installed equipment, and its contract, value and data-access terms are unpublished.

summary: An [e-Justice platform is deployed in one court, with five judicial procedures digitised and more than 40 justice-sector professionals trained](2026-08-25-undp-senegal-e-justice-dakar-pilot).
developments:
2026-08-24 — the Justice Minister and the UN development agency's resident representative [discussed the digital transformation of the Pikine-Guediawaye courthouse in the Dakar suburbs, where the e-Justice programme is being extended](2026-08-25-undp-senegal-e-justice-dakar-pilot). The programme's final report records five judicial procedures digitised, the platform deployed in that one court and more than 40 justice-sector professionals trained, following a July 2025 installation of a mini data centre, a network connection to Dakar, a backup site and end-user equipment.

What the base does not hold is any extension beyond the single court: a roadmap for possible expansion exists and no further courts are announced, and plans to integrate the Maisons de justice and Boutiques de droit are stated but not dated. No case volume, clearance time or user figure is published for the digitised procedures, so the deployment is recorded and its effect is not. The account is the supporting agency's own.
